subject: PHI ingestion: encryption, residency & KMS options

Subject: PHI ingestion: encryption, residency & KMS options

Hi Katie / Michael —

Thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap of what we discussed and suggested next steps so we stay aligned. I pasted the short action list below and attached the security questionnaire (Obsidian_Security_Questions.xlsx) for reference.

Recap (high level)
- Data types: PHI (signed consent forms + diagnostic metadata), low-volume episodic uploads from clinics.
- Residency: Must remain in US (customer req), ideally US-East region.
- Encryption: In-transit TLS 1.2/1.3; at-rest AES-256.
- Key management options we proposed:
  1) Redwood-managed keys (default) — easiest, no key material exchange.
  2) Customer-managed keys via Cloud KMS (bring your own key policy; Redwood integrates with customer's KMS role).
  3) HSM-backed BYOK (importable keys or wrapped key exchange; we can support HSM-based key custody for highest assurance).
- Logging & retention: Audit logs retained for 1 year by default; can extend to 3/7 years on Dedicated. Event-level telemetry includes request id, model/version, token counts (no raw prompt storage unless configured).

Questions you raised
- HSM certification: whether imported keys retain FIPS 140-2/3 posture (see attachments and answer below).
- Latency/regression concerns if we route to a Dedicated cluster with CMK/HSM flow.
- Evidence for procurement (SOC 2 controls, KMS integration diagram).

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep dive: schedule 60m with Redwood infra + security (include Ben Carter, our security lead on the thread) to walk HSM key flow and latency implications.
2) Provide HSM import options doc + FIPS attestations (we'll attach our HSM partner docs).
3) Draft a minimal mutual action plan: Dedicated pilot (2 GPUs), residency in us-east-1, CMK via Obsidian's cloud KMS; procurement to confirm SLA & pricing.
4) Obsidian to fill the attached security questionnaire and return — we'll use this to populate the compliance packet for legal review.

Attachments: Obsidian_Security_Questions.xlsx, PHI_network_diagram.png

I'll propose slots for the deep dive once I hear back on availability. Thanks again —

Thanks Lauren — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we book the deep dive: 

1) HSM / FIPS: We need to confirm that keys stored in the HSM retain FIPS 140-2/3 compliance and that key import/export processes meet our internal audit. Do you have the partner attestation and the exact import workflow?

2) Key ownership model: For Cloud KMS BYOK, does Redwood ever have the ability to unwrap or export the customer key? We need explicit confirmation that key material remains under our control.

3) Latency: If we add a HSM step for every key operation, does that add a measurable latency penalty during inference (cold starts / new session handshakes)? We cannot accept a 100–200ms p50 regression for our synchronous API calls.

4) Logs & PII: We need to ensure no unmasked PHI is stored in logs or transient telemetry. Can you confirm tokenization/redaction behaviors in the default hosted flow vs dedicated?

Availability for the deep dive this week: Wed 10/13 10–12 PT or Thu 10/14 9–11 PT. Adding legal (legal@obsidian-health.com) if they want to join the call.

—Katie

Subject: Re: PHI ingestion: encryption, residency & KMS options

Katie — thanks, great questions. Short answers below; we can go deeper on the call.

1) HSM / FIPS: Redwood integrates with HSM partners that provide FIPS 140-2 level 3 attestations. We will share the vendor attestation PDF and the whitepaper describing key import/backup/zeroization. In summary: when using HSM-backed BYOK, the key material is generated or imported into the HSM and the raw material never leaves the HSM in plaintext.

2) Key ownership: For Cloud KMS and HSM BYOK modes, Redwood operates under a least-privilege KMS role. We do not retain unwrapped key material. For KMS integrations our standard flow is: customer creates key in their KMS; grants Redwood a limited decrypt/encrypt-only role via IAM; Redwood stores only the KMS key identifier and uses the KMS for crypto operations. We will include an architecture diagram on the call.

3) Latency: Normal inference request paths are not synchronous to the HSM for every token. We use a session-level wrapped key and in-memory enclave/KV cache so per-token generation does not call the KMS/HSM. The primary latency impact is at session creation / cold start and for periodic key rotation ops. Typical added latency at session init is ~15–25ms dependent on region/partner (we will measure during the pilot). We will capture p50/p95 estimates during the Dedicated pilot.

4) Logs & PII: Default hosted logging scrubs raw prompt/response content from long-term storage unless explicitly enabled. For Dedicated we can configure no persistent prompt retention and only emit structured telemetry (request IDs, token counts, model id) to logs. We'll mark this in the mutual action plan.

Next steps:
- Ben Carter (cc'd) — can you gather the HSM partner attestation pack and the internal architecture diagram for KMS/HSM flows?
- Katie / Obsidian — confirm Wed 10/13 10–11 PT or Thu 10/14 9–10 PT. Will send calendar invite with agenda (attestation pack + latency baseline + pilot scope).

Thanks —
Lauren
